content:
Connor O'Brien: Looking for final go/no-go on enabling `batching_tier=standard` by default (i.e., for customers who have NOT explicitly set tier/knobs) for the initial hosted cohort. Target is runtime-1.21 flag ramp today.

Connor O'Brien: Cohort as discussed: Hosted API only, regions `us-east-1` + `eu-west-1`, models: `llama-3.1-70b-instruct` + `qwen2.5-32b-instruct`. Dedicated/Private unaffected (explicit config continues to override; helm values keep current behavior).

ReleaseBot: CI status for release/runtime-1.21: ✅ unit ✅ e2e ✅ perf-canary (tiered) ✅

Sofia Ivanova: Runtime side: scheduler changes are in 1.21, tier mapping behind `tiered_batching_defaults_enabled` flag. Effective-config endpoint is live in staging. No open perf regressions on the perf-canary jobs since the decode prioritization fix.

Allison Grant: Observability: dashboards are updated and verified against staging + canary. We have per-tier views for p50/p95/p99, queue delay histograms, batch size distribution, and timeout/cancel. Alert rules are scoped to the cohort models/regions.

Sean Gallagher: SLO policy: for standard tier, paging threshold is p95 latency regression >15% for 15m compared to 7d baseline OR timeout rate >0.3% for 10m (route-level) OR 5xx >0.2% for 10m. Also watching queue delay p99; we don’t page on it alone but it’s an early warning.

Rafael Mendes: On-call/SRE: we’re good with the ramp if rollback is crisp. Confirming rollback mechanisms:
1) flag flip to 0% in control plane (should take <2 min)
2) model registry tier default version revert (if needed) for affected models
3) if we see overload interaction issues, we can also tighten overload protection thresholds without touching tier mapping

Connor O'Brien: Yep. Rollback playbook in the checklist doc is up to date (same as last beta ramp). Owners: Rafael primary, Connor secondary for flag ops.

Aditya Rao: Product: +1 to proceeding. This is the “standard by default” step we committed to, and we’re keeping the opt-out simple (`batching_tier=fast` or explicit knobs). Docs are already merged and live for tier explanation + FAQ.

Chloe Martin: Console: tier dropdown is visible for the cohort, and we show “effective config” with a link to the explain endpoint payload. This should help Support w/ the “why did my latency change” questions.

Benji Okafor: Flagging details: `tiered_batching_defaults_enabled` supports percentage by {model, region}. I’ve precreated the cohorts. Proposed schedule:
- 5% for 30m
- 25% for 2h
- 100% for remaining traffic if clean
We can pause at any step.

Rafael Mendes: For auto-rollback, are we using the hooks from 18515? (i.e., canary monitor triggers revert to previous cohort config)

Connor O'Brien: Yes, but we’re keeping a human-in-the-loop today. Auto-rollback is armed for hard thresholds (timeouts + 5xx), not for p95 variance. If it trips, it will set cohort percent to 0 and page #eng-sre + #eng-releases.

Sean Gallagher: One nuance: for long-context spikes, standard tier should be safer than cost-efficient, but queue delay can still blow up if we get concurrency surge. Make sure the abort condition includes “queue delay p99 > 120ms for 10m” as a stop-the-ramp signal (not an auto rollback).

Allison Grant: Added as a “stop ramp” panel + annotation on the dashboard. Also added a quick view filtered to streaming routes since cadence issues were the earlier concern.

Sofia Ivanova: Streaming: fast tier fix remains; standard tier uses conservative decode weight. In the last characterization run, token cadence p95 stayed within tolerance. If we see TTFT drift, likely due to queue delay -> we’ll know quickly.

Connor O'Brien: Confirming: Dedicated/Private not affected unless customer opts in, correct?

Sofia Ivanova: Correct. Precedence is: explicit knobs > explicit tier > deployment-level default > model registry default > runtime baseline. This change only alters the default tier when nothing is set (hosted cohort only).

Aditya Rao: Support readiness: we have the “effective config” guidance + a short troubleshooting snippet. If any tickets come in, we’ll route through #support + #eng-sre with the new headers (tier + effective params) attached.

Rafael Mendes: Ok. Go from SRE. Please post the dashboard link + checklist link in #eng-sre when you start the 5% ramp.

Connor O'Brien: Great. Final go/no-go poll here:
- Runtime (Sofia)?
- SRE (Rafael/Sean)?
- Product (Aditya)?

Sofia Ivanova: Go.

Sean Gallagher: Go.

Rafael Mendes: Go.

Aditya Rao: Go.

Benji Okafor: Go, flag ready.

Connor O'Brien: ✅ Decision: GO. Starting 5% ramp now for (us-east-1, eu-west-1) + (llama-3.1-70b, qwen2.5-32b). Will update this thread at 30m / 2h marks with metrics + any issues. Rollback owner on point: Rafael; backup: Connor.

Connor O'Brien: Also: if we have to abort ramp, we pause at current %, flip to 0 if needed, and we’ll file a short retro note in the runtime-1.21 launch brief.

Rafael Mendes: Sounds good. Watching dashboards now.
